title: Session Cohesion & Prefetch Playbook — PRD Ideation
summary: Working PRD sketch focused on reducing tail latency and developer friction for long-lived interactive sessions. Proposes a lightweight session cohesion model (resume tokens + epoched checkpoints), a prefetch manifest for downstream tool residency and model variants, and SDK ergonomics to surface these controls to integrators without breaking simple call patterns. Draft is intentionally pragmatic: propose an initial minimal surface that we can A/B and iterate on with real teams.
goals: Cut 95th/99th percentile response time for multi-step interactive flows by enabling proactive prefetching and lightweight resume
Provide a predictable, opt-in semantic for tool residency so SDKs can avoid cold RPCs during critical interaction windows
Keep the core hosted API ergonomics simple for 80% of users while exposing advanced knobs to power teams
Ship telemetry hooks to attribute unit-cost changes to prefetch decisions and tool residency
non_goals: Replace existing session storage or introduce heavy stateful server owners — should be stateless-friendly
Tightly couple client SDK versions with server-side rollout entitlements
Build on-prem-only primitives in the first cut — focus on hosted API first
user_stories: As a knowledge-assistant developer, I want the session to resume quickly after a brief network drop so users don’t wait for cold model inference
As a developer using tool calls (search, code-run), I want the SDK to keep a tool stub warm during a user session so latency-sensitive calls avoid cold RPCs
As a platform engineer, I want to measure how many prefetches were used vs wasted so we can tune cost/latency tradeoffs
As an SDK consumer, I want the simple generate/chat APIs to work unchanged unless I opt into advanced session features
key_requirements: Lightweight resume tokens returned on session creation and any stable checkpoint (opaque token that encodes last-seen epoch and a signed TTL)
Prefetch manifest: client-specified hints for model variants, tool proxies, and asset bundles with soft priorities
Tool residency hints: small lease semantics (e.g., keep tool warm for N seconds) with server guidance on cost impact
Non-blocking prefetch API: prefetch requests are advisory and may be throttled; client must be able to proceed without prefetch completion
Structured output schema versioning: responses can include a compact ‘delta schemas’ payload for partial JSON/schemas to allow client-side incremental parsing
Observability tags on each request indicating whether it hit prefetched state / resume path or cold path
Backward compatibility: if client doesn’t send prefetch hints, behavior defaults to current hosted API
api_primitives: POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/prefetch => manifest payload (models, tools, assets, priority)
POST /v1/resume => resume_token => attempts to rehydrate session KV/cache on server-side fast-path
streaming delta frames: typed partials that include "schema_hint" and "commit" flags
tool-lease header: x-rw-tool-lease: <seconds> on prefetch calls to request warm residency
sdk_ergonomics_notes: SDKs should expose a minimal opt-in: Session.create() returns a small Session object with .prefetch(manifest, opts) and an automatic lightweight heartbeat while the app foregrounds the session. Default behavior: no prefetch. Advanced mode: sessionAffinity=true which pipes hints to the server. Keep sync and streaming APIs identical; prefetch/resume are additive. Mobile SDKs: provide a small on-device cache of last resume token and allow background prefetch with strict bandwidth/cost guardrails.
streaming_behavior_notes: Partial frames use a compact envelope: {frame_type, schema_hint, payload_fragment, commit_flag}. Clients should be able to assemble partial JSON/NDJSON lines without blocking final commit. If a resume token is used mid-stream we try to replay prefix KV then continue streaming; fallen-back events must be annotated. There should be a small ack mechanism for important commits (non-blocking by default).
tool_calling_patterns: We prefer a residency-first model for high-frequency tool calls: a short-lived warm lease is requested from prefetch and the server may respond with a tool_proxy_id that short-circuits later RPCs. Tools retain a small transitory cache keyed by tool_proxy_id. Tool calls not covered by residency degrade gracefully to regular RPC. Consider adding a fast-hedge path: if tool_latency > threshold, automatically route to fallback tool variant.
structured_output_guidelines: Encourage schema-first answers for integrations (ex: {type: 'action', action: {...}}). Provide a compact schema-hinting mechanism in partial frames so clients can parse incrementally. Define versioned schema identifiers and a tolerant parser spec: missing fields produce warnings, not failures. Offer an optional post-commit validation hook in console to show regressions for schema changes.
telemetry_and_rollout: Emit the following tags per request: session_id (opt), resume_path: [cache|prefetch|cold], prefetch_manifest_id, tool_lease_used(boolean), schema_version. Add counters for prefetch_issued, prefetch_used, prefetch_expired, resume_success, resume_fallback. Rollout plan: gated alpha (internal + two external customers) -> beta (selected customers) -> general availability. For alpha only: allow force-prefetch feature flag to measure waste. Collect cost attribution in experiment buckets.
open_questions: How do we sign/rotate resume_tokens for private deployments (must work for Private and Dedicated)?
What is acceptable TTL for tool leases before cost becomes prohibitive? 10s, 30s, 120s?
Should prefetch be billable separately or included in normal request billing? (opt: explicit prefetch billing for transparency)
What's the exact shape of the minimal manifest so low-bandwidth clients can use it?
How to reconcile prefetch state with model rollouts / canary changes?
risks_and_mitigations: Cost bloat from aggressive prefetching => mitigation: default off, server-side budget scoring, prefetch budget per account
Privacy leakage via resume token reuse => mitigation: short TTLs + signed tokens + per-customer keys in Private mode
Increased system complexity and harder debugging => mitigation: strong telemetry, sampling of prefetch traces, debug-mode replay tools
SDK fragmentation (different behavior across platforms) => mitigation: ship reference JS and mobile SDKs with same semantic defaults and strict test harness
